entry.title: ROLI Enters Administration
entry.content:
Links: musictech.com | wired.com

Music technology company ROLI has entered administration for the second time, with insolvency practitioners from RSM UK appointed as joint administrators. The sudden collapse has left numerous customers with unfulfilled orders, unresponsive support, and offline web and community servers.

Founded in 2009 and renowned for pioneering MIDI Polyphonic Expression (MPE) alongside touch-sensitive instruments like the Seaboard and Airwave, ROLI previously survived administration in 2021 before restructuring. The company's latest failure has raised concerns among users that a lack of ongoing software and firmware support could eventually render their hardware devices unusable.

entry.content:

Electronic music pioneer and Belleville Three co-founder Juan Atkins died on October 31, 2026, at the age of 64 in Mexico City, where he was scheduled to perform. Tributes from across the global electronic music community poured in following the news, celebrating his foundational role in shaping the techno genre.

Emerging from Detroit in the late 1970s and early 1980s, Atkins helped establish the blueprint for techno through his pioneering work with projects like Cybotron and Model 500, as well as his Metroplex record label. His fusion of futuristic synthesizer sounds, drum machines like the Roland TR-808, and speculative fiction profoundly influenced generations of electronic music producers worldwide.

entry.title: DiscImageStudio Open-Source Tool Burns Visible Artwork Onto CDs, DVDs, and Blu-ray Discs
entry.content:
Links: github.com | hacker news

DiscImageStudio is an open-source software utility that converts standard images into data aligned with the physical constraints of CDs, DVDs, and single-layer BD-R discs, enabling users to burn visible artwork directly onto disc surfaces. It provides a Windows desktop application featuring layer-based design tools, grayscale adjustment, and direct streaming or image export, alongside experimental command-line interfaces for Linux and macOS.

The application incorporates precise auxiliary calibration algorithms to correct track geometry, supports hybrid file directory mapping, and exports standard formats such as ISO, RAW, and WAV+CUE. Built on .NET 10, the tool references physical specifications from ECMA and ISO/IEC to accurately translate image pixels into physical disc tracks and error correction codes while operating offline without telemetry.

entry.content:
Links: bedroomproducersblog.com | zl-audio.github.io

ZL Audio has released ZL Limiter, a free and open-source audio limiter plugin available for Windows, macOS, and Linux. The software features True Peak limiting and oversampling up to 32x to help control inter-sample peaks and reduce aliasing during audio production.

The plugin is provided in common formats like VST3, Audio Unit, and LV2 to accommodate various digital audio workstations. Developed as an open-source tool, its source code and packaging are hosted on GitHub for user inspection and community contribution.

entry.title: NeuSynth Mac Plugin Released for Exploring Alternative Instrument Stems
entry.content:
Links: bedroomproducersblog.com | neusynth.com

NeuSynth is a macOS audio plugin designed to help producers test alternative instrument parts against an existing track. Users drag up to 60 seconds of audio from their digital audio workstation into the plugin, select instrument categories, provide reference tracks, or describe desired parts using text prompts.

The plugin generates four distinct variation sets, each delivered as separate WAV files that can be previewed in context and dragged directly into a project session. NeuSynth operates on a credit-based system, offering a free trial alongside monthly subscription plans and top-up options for commercial use.

entry.title: StageBox Software Releases Voiks Toy Keyboard Sampler Plugin
entry.content:
Links: bedroomproducersblog.com | stageboxsoftware.com

StageBox Software has released Voiks, a free lo-fi sampler plugin for macOS and Windows inspired by the 1987 Yamaha VSS-30 sampling keyboard. The instrument allows users to record audio through an interface or load audio files, automatically detecting root notes and mapping the sample across the keyboard.

The plugin includes modern features such as stereo sample support, recordings up to 30 seconds long, sound overdubbing, and patch saving that embeds audio data directly. Additional sound-shaping tools include an ADSR envelope, filters, modulation, and a dedicated tweaks section for adjusting converter character, sample rate, and bit depth.
